title: Selby St James Halifax Memorial
location_name: St James the Apostle Church, Selby, North Yorkshire
memorial_details: Plaque and memorabilia display in St James the Apostle Church, Selby, including the original cockerel weather vane 'grounded' since the church spire was never rebuilt after the crash.
narrative: Halifax JB789 of 1658 Heavy Conversion Unit departed Riccall at an unknown time and, for unknown reasons, struck the spire of St James the Apostle Church in Selby at 0102 on 9 May 1944, then crashed into a town-centre residential street. All seven crew were killed. Seven civilians on the ground also died; a further seven were seriously injured, one of whom died later. The original cockerel weather vane from the spire, which was never rebuilt, is now preserved in the church as a memorial.
cause_of_loss: Struck church spire during night cross-country training exercise; crashed into residential street
community_connection: Seven civilians in Selby were killed when the aircraft struck the church spire and fell into a residential street. A further seven were seriously injured. The church spire was never rebuilt; the original cockerel weather vane is preserved in the church.
